text:
24-hour news summary.

1. AI robotics models may soon achieve real-time performance close to Astra through rapid prefill improvements and distillation. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5489)
2. Cline released Pixel Canary, a free stealth model that ties GPT-6 Astra and outperforms Kimi K3 on Next.js Agent Evals. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5490)
3. Eyecandy Robotics launched to bring animated characters to life through robotics and AI. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5491)
4. Ukraine announced an “Army of Robots” initiative, building on its drone industry and aiming to advance the robotization of warfare. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5492)
5. Bill Gates warned that AI could drive events causing a billion deaths. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5493)
6. Jensen Huang argued that forgetting skills such as long division, multiplication tables, and square roots may not matter in the AI era. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5494)
7. Derek Guy argued that math education matters for rigorous thinking and evaluating causal claims, which are essential to a functioning democracy. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5495)
8. A speech urged software engineers and everyone else to preserve happy memories, face reality, and remain optimistic about the future. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5496)
9. Linkerbot showcased its seven-axis LinkerArm A7 moving as one. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5497)
10. Robots can perform highly dynamic actions such as cracking a whip or lassoing a cleat by directly copying human motion capture, without learning. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5498)
11. Lukas Petersson predicted that AI will understand physical 3D space better than humans by the end of the year. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5499)
12. A demonstration of Opus 5.5 showed it recognizing dotted lines and filling in a missing arm, raising concerns about its capabilities. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5500)
13. Geoffrey Hinton called for stronger government AI regulation, saying standards are insufficient and major AI companies oppose proposed rules. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5501)
14. OpenAI, Anthropic, and security researchers are investigating tens of thousands of potentially problematic incidents involving frontier models. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5502)

--Hermes
